# P36.18 — Layout and chrome (UXK14-2)

**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/358_P36.18__layout-and-chrome.md`
(manifest row **358**, Round 11 / P36, sub-round 11C). **Requirement ids
satisfied:** SIG-UI-051 (*Six-section navigation* — the header offers at
most six sections plus a search field, and a section or menu item renders
only when its target route exists in the release being served — enforced
by the computed release route manifest, never a hand list), SIG-UI-145
(*Forty-word chrome* — the shared chrome's visible-by-default strings are

SIG-UI-044 module stays one action away behind a native disclosure and is
page-specific on record pages), SIG-UI-150 (*Header and menu* — ≤ 6
sections + search, `aria-current` on the current section, the header and
`main` share one grid, mobile collapses to a no-JavaScript `<details>`

elsewhere):** SIG-UI-039 (the T-page contract — chrome ships no scripts
on T0/T1, proven unchanged), SIG-UI-040 (the ADR-155 page-type posture —
37 public + 13 internal routes classified, none re-typed),
SIG-ENG-042 (the manifest fails closed: a section whose routes are absent
is omitted, never a dead link; an unfilled `{slot}` in a chrome template
is a build error). **Carried decisions, verbatim:** C-31 — **"Six
sections (UXR-01): Watch is top-level (advocate A2 and organizer O2
primary task); Sources & data holds Sources, Evidence, Downloads & API,
Releases & changes, Status; About holds How sure is SIG? (`/quality/`)
and Open questions; Disagreements sits under Explore. The queue is
reached mainly from absence chips and 'What we don't know' (UXR-29)"**
and `D-K14-4 = yes` (no dark-mode toggle in Round 11 — none added);
`D-K14-2 = yes` (the name stays "Surveillance Infrastructure Graph
(SIG)" — the wordmark carries it).
**Outreach-owed check (ADR-171) — unmet:** this row sends no outreach —
no outside contact.
**Base:** `8938aa50` (tip of `r11/P36.17-lexicon-and-copy-system`) ·
**Branch:** `r11/P36.18-layout-and-chrome` ·

## Why

The shared chrome had drifted from the design: K14 measured roughly 138
visible chrome words, **15 header links** in three groups with no
current-page marker (`aria-current` count: 0), and the mobile H1
starting **344 px** down the phone screen — 41 % of the viewport gone
before the page names itself. The nav also offered routes the release
may not serve: nothing kept the menu honest against what the build
actually emits. This row lands K14 UXK14-2 with the K13 IA: a compact,
route-aware, zero-JavaScript chrome shell every page shares.

## What ships

- **`web/src/lib/release-routes.ts`** — the release route manifest: the
  set of public routes THIS build serves, computed at build from the
  emitted page files (`import.meta.glob` over `src/pages/` — robust in
  dev, vitest and the prerender bundle) plus data-conditioned probes
  (`dossier/unplaced/` only when the unplaced report exists) and, in
  `export` mode, the pipeline's declared `<exportDir>/web/site-routes.json`
  (`sig.site-routes/1`). Internal surfaces live outside the glob — they
  can never enter the manifest. A nav target that names an absent route
  never renders (UXR-01, SIG-ENG-042).
- **`web/src/lib/nav.ts`** — the six K13 §2.1 sections in canonical
  order (Places · Explore · Watch · Organizations · Sources & data ·
  About), every declared item filtered against the manifest, a section
  omitted when nothing in it resolves, the landing label falling back
  to the first resolvable item, and `aria-current` wiring — longest
  prefix match so the current section is marked on the desktop bar and
  the mobile menu alike.
- **`web/src/components/chrome/`** — `SiteHeader.astro` (wordmark,
  sections, the search entry as a plain GET to `/search/`, the mobile
  `<details>` menu carrying the same filtered sections — no JavaScript
  anywhere), `Breadcrumbs.astro` (ordered trail in a labelled nav; the
  last crumb unlinked with `aria-current="page"`), `PageHeaderBand.astro`
  (the shared band: crumbs, H1, optional lede, the release stamp line,
  page actions, and the Cite `<details>` holding the full citation
  affordance — SIG-UI-035 one action away inside the word budget).
- **`BaseLayout.astro` rewired** — the 15-link grouped nav and the
  bare `<h1>` + bottom-of-page provenance module are replaced by the
  header, the band, and the footer strip: the "Built from N sources ·
  data as of … · {reviewStatus}" line with Dispute one step away, the
  full module + release sentences + publication basis inside the
  `<details>`, the route-aware footer link row (licences, status today —
  About/Contact/Releases/resources declared, rendered when the routes
  exist), and the "not a census · not advocacy" tagline.
- **Dossier breadcrumbs + actions** — `dossier/[...path].astro` passes
  the canonical chain (country > state > county > place — flat legacy
  dossiers render Places > `<name>`, never an unverified ancestry) and
  the band actions (Print/JSON — `links.print`-gated as before, now
  `withBase()`-joined).
- **`lexicon.chrome`** — every visible-by-default chrome string in the
  lexicon (SIG-UI-145): the strip template carries `{sources}` /
  `{asOf}` / `{reviewStatus}` slots filled from build data — a
  hard-coded count or date is a lint failure, not a copy edit. The
  `check-lexicon` "chrome" leg counts the declared words: **31 ≤ 40**.
- **Mobile bar (K14 §5.3)** — ≤ 56 px: wordmark mark, a compact search
  link to `/search/`, the Menu `<details>`; breadcrumbs stay one line
  (the current crumb ellipsises — the H1 repeats the title below).
  Mobile H1 top ≈ 100 px at 320 px (from 344), asserted ≤ 120 px.
- **Root-absolute baseline shrunk 157 → 141** — the header's hard-coded
  hrefs are gone; every new link goes through `withBase()`. The
  regenerated baseline is recorded (shrink only, P36.66a).
- **Post-review fix (head `df2d0ee8`): `/network/` island-mount CLS** —
  the first head-bound run's Lighthouse leg measured
  `cumulative-layout-shift` 0.0687 on all three runs against the ≤ 0.05
  ceiling. The graph island mounts ~95 rem tall at the 412 px budget
  viewport inside a ~150 px section and pushed the lists below ~1,500 px
  — the same defect the map's `sig-island__placeholder` already fixes.
  The explorer now carries the same pattern (stepped `min-height`
  95/85/73 rem from fixtures-build measurements; `:has()` hides it on
  mount; an honest note stays for JavaScript-off readers): local
  `check:perf` re-run green, `/network/` CLS 0.000 ×3. The commit also
  adds the `## [Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry the `docs` job's
  SIG-REL-014 gate requires for this row's public-behaviour paths.
- **Post-review fix (national byte bounds): `measured_gaps` records** —
  the records head's national wire-measure read `/network/`
  `totalInitialMaxBytes` 1,900,589 B past the recorded 1,900,000 B
  regression bound (+589) and `/search/` `totalInitialMaxBytes`
  192,259 B past the ratified 184,320 B ceiling: this row's shared
  chrome adds ≈ 4.5 KB gz to every page's initial transfer and carried

  D-P35.51-3 (measure 1,900,589, bound 1,920,000) and a new
  national-scoped `/search/` row records under D-P35.51-2 — the React

  budgets re-run 47/47 green, fixtures 47/47 green.
- **Chain repair (row-354 defect, heads `fd03faa8`/`30aad87f`)** — the
  `python` job on `26e54b77` (run 40624323150, started 03:01Z) failed
  `test_check_dry_run_is_green_without_adc[rate-limit-enforcement.sh]`:
  `leg_flip`'s AR-3 window guard correctly refuses `--check` inside the
  daily 03:00–06:30Z freeze (exit 42), and the generic dry-run sweep
  asserted exit 0 at any wall-clock time — every in-window `python` job
  on any head fails until repaired. Fixed with the script's documented
  test seam: `SIG_RATELIMIT_NOW` pinned to `2026-10-20T12:00:00Z`
  (outside the freeze and all three declared AR-3 batch windows;
  past-dated so the future-literal guard is silent). The refusal
  contract itself stands — this is the script's own seam, not a
  relaxation.

## Deviations / deferrals

1. **`/network/` stands in for "Graph explorer"** — SIG-UI-051 names the
   canonical item; `/explore/` is a later row's route (today's network
   surface is the graph explorer). The item is declared for both routes
   so a release serving `/explore/` lights it without a code change.
2. **Organizations honestly absent** — no `/entity/` route exists, so
   the section does not render (the requirement's own rule). Declared;
   it lights when GX-06a ships the hub.
3. **A–Z not offered** — `/dossier/a-z/<l>/` is a parameterized family,
   not a route a menu can name; JUR-04 owns it.
4. **`release-routes.ts` uses `import.meta.glob`, not fs** — a
   filesystem walk anchored on `import.meta.url` resolves inside
   `dist/.prerender/` at build; the glob keys exist identically in all
   runtimes. Declared-site-routes (`site-routes.json`) is the
   pipeline-declared extension point for export builds.
5. **Deferrals: +0/−0** — nothing unlandable; no live leg, no
   production mutation.

## Test plan

- Removing a section, offering an absent route, dropping `aria-current`,
  hard-coding a chrome word or count, or shipping a dead menu link each
  fails a named check (`check:lexicon` chrome leg, `navForRoutes` unit
  tests, `release-routes` manifest tests, `chrome-nav.spec.ts`) — every
  new behaviour carries a fails-if-removed test.
- ADR-155: no route's classification changed (37 public + 13 internal
  classified at build); chrome adds zero scripts — T0 stays script-free,
  T1 keeps no-JS parity (the `<details>` affordances are native HTML),
  T2 budgets unchanged.
